standard: Field Assembly Record Standard 1.2, §8 market records; see PROVENANCE.md
notes: DRAFT, not reviewed, not signed. Numbers computed from run 2026-11-16T134201Z. The BLS PPI, CPI and average-price series carry October 2026. Prose drafted 2026-11-16 by a session from numbers.md and numbers.json, modeled on Issue 1; one drafting pass; tools/check.py passes at 187 figures. Recalculated by the drafting session from the retained captures of the issue run, not from numbers.json, and all matched: from ams_pork_cutout/json.json, for the carcass cutout and each of the six primals, the week ending 2026-11-06 and its year-earlier week ending 2025-11-07, the four weekly values ending 2026-10-16, 10-23, 10-30 and 11-06 and the four ending 2025-10-17, 10-24, 10-31 and 11-07, both four-week simple averages and both percent changes; the printed PDF of report 2680 (dated 2026-11-09) agrees on the latest week's seven values and on its week-over-week changes; from bls/series.json, both PPIs for 2026-10, 2025-10 and 2024-10 and their changes, and the 2026-10 and 2024-10 values and two-year changes of both CPI-U series and both average prices; from nass_hogs_pigs/archive_txt.txt (hgpg0926.txt, released 2026-09-24), the September 1 2025 and 2026 counts for all hogs and pigs, kept for breeding, market, and 180 pounds and over; from usda_ers_fpo/cpi_csv.csv, the pork, meats and food-away-from-home year-over-year and 2027 interval attributes. Comparisons that do not exist: BLS marks 2025-10 with value '-' and footnote 'Data unavailable due to the 2025 lapse in appropriations' for CUUR0000SEFD, CUUR0000SEFV, APU0000FD3101 and APU0000704111 in the retained series.json, so the pork CPI, food-away-from-home CPI, sliced bacon and pork chops rows carry no year-earlier value; the issue names all four in the read, under the table, in the uncertainty and in the record. The two PPI series carry 2025-10 values. The hog inventory carries no two-year comparison. Comparison with Issue 1 is made in words only (a fall is larger or smaller than the one Issue 1 reported), because Issue 1's figures are not in this computed set; those statements were checked by hand against the published Issue 1 table, and the week ending 2026-10-09 values in this run's capture equal the ones Issue 1 printed. Known limits carried into the text. The cutout and primals are for the week ending 2026-11-06, published 2026-11-09; the run was on Monday 2026-11-16 and the week ending 2026-11-13 was not yet in the source. The beef computed set for 2026-11 reaches the week ending 2026-11-13, so this title reads one week behind beef. The cheddar computed set for 2026-11 carries CME weeks ending 2026-11-06, the same week as this cutout, so the issue says pork is behind beef and level with cheddar this month, not behind both. The pork cutout is comprehensive (all sales types and delivery periods); the beef cutout is negotiated sales delivered within 0-21 days. The cutout and primals are estimated values per 100 pounds FOB plant on a 215-pound barrow and gilt carcass, not the price of any cut. NASS figures are head, not prices, and are the same September release Issue 1 used; in this run the source status is OK (archive copy fetched, rolling Todays_Reports path recorded SKIPPED, not tried). The October PPIs are preliminary. The USDA ERS attributes are September to September, from the update of 2026-10-23. Month-to-month movement is not in the computed set. The weekly pork variety meat report is retained and not parsed. Bare counts and worded quantities the gate does not read, checked by hand against the captures and the computed set: six primals; the single-week fall larger than in Issue 1 for the carcass and all six primals; the four-week fall larger for the carcass and four primals (ham, picnic, loin, rib) and smaller for the belly and the butt; both PPI falls larger than Issue 1's; the slaughter hog index above its level of two years earlier in Issue 1 and below it now; the carcass cutout falling in every one of the four weeks; the ham the only primal to rise in the latest week and the latest week the only one of its four in which it rose; the rib the highest and the picnic the lowest primal value; the two groups of three primals and their ranges on both comparisons; four consumer series without a year-earlier value; five kinds of measure; the product specification quoted from report 2680 (215-pound carcass, 55 to 56 percent lean, 0.55 to 0.70 inches backfat, Monday to Friday, one-to-one carcass averaging); the NASS reliability sentence (largest first-to-latest difference over 20 quarters, 1,836 thousand, exceeds this year's change of 1,136 thousand); 'more than ten weeks old' for a September 1 count read on November 16; the next NASS release date of 2026-12-23, from the retained ESMIS landing page; the 52-week and four-day comparison rule; 0 to 21 days for beef. Open points for the editor. (1) The September 2026 reading of WPU02210444 is 100.469 in this run's series.json against 100.443 in the 2026-10-18 run, so Issue 1's printed 100.4 would now print 100.5; the draft says the reading changed without restating it, and whether Issue 1 needs a note is the editor's call. (2) The cheddar point above differs from the standing note that pork runs a week behind beef and cheddar. (3) The draft states that the falls were recalculated from the retained file and matched; keep or cut. (4) The sentence that a later run will not fill the October 2025 gap unless BLS publishes those values is a statement about the source's behavior. (5) Next issue is worded without a date because no retained capture holds the BLS release date for November PPI. (6) numbers.md omits the 'Market hogs and pigs' row that numbers.json holds as hogs_market; the issue table carries it, as Issue 1's did. (7) evidence.json lists every fetch of the issue run, including the SKIPPED NASS rolling path; nothing the issue rests on is missing from it. Independent review 2026-11-16 (a separate session pass that recalculated every headline figure, date and weekday from the captures; all matched numbers.json; all eight evidence.json hashes re-checked; every worded comparison with Issue 1 checked against its published table and found right). Applied: the primal grouping sentence corrected (the butt, rib, loin order is the same on both comparisons; only ham and picnic change places); the statements about the beef and cheddar weeks attributed to those titles' November computed sets and evidence files, and the beef cutout specification attributed to the Beef Monitor's methodology; the BLS revision sentence made complete (August as well as September WPU02210444 differ from the October issue's file: September 100.443 to 100.469, August 106.794 to 106.822; Issue 1's printed 100.4 would now print 100.5, its -28.3% and -20.8% unchanged at printed precision) and tied to run 2026-10-18T145155Z; the record section no longer claims evidence.json covers the cross-issue and cross-title statements; the BLS scope narrowed to the four series this title carries; 'does not exist' made 'does not exist in the BLS series'; 'NASS revises' made 'may revise' (the release says estimates 'are subject to revision when current estimates are made'; Issue 1 carries the stronger wording); the publication page named as ESMIS; 'for this draft' made 'before publication'. Left for the editor: the cross-title sentences name the Beef Monitor's and Cheddar Check's November sets, which are themselves drafts; if either publishes on a different run those sentences need rechecking.
